- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (especially in 30d horizon), model exhibits mean reversion bias; adjust downward by 1–4% for next forecast.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model often fails to recognize trend continuation; forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–3% to match true path.  
- If model forecast is >5% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive periods, apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period to avoid overconfidence in momentum.  
- In low-sentiment, low-price regimes (e.g., <40), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment remains neutral or mildly negative.
